persona.who: 29, chartered accountant in Indore, married 1 year, lives with in-laws who expect her to give up the practice after a baby. Husband avoids the topic.
persona.note: my mother in law keeps saying once the baby comes you will anyway leave all this CA work. I built my practice from zero. my husband just changes the subject. I feel like I am slowly being erased

understanding.bridge: What you are living with is what the texts call being seen as less than you are, and that is where this week begins.
understanding.week_thesis: Seven days from being told you will be erased to standing in the life you built, with the words to say so.

week_beats.hook: You recognise being told you will be erased, and the quiet beside it, named without blame.

understanding.core_struggle: A woman who built her CA practice from zero is being told she will leave it after the baby, while her husband stays silent.
understanding.mirror: You built this practice from nothing, and now you're being told it ends with the baby.
understanding.insight: You are not asking for too much. You are being handed a smaller picture of yourself than the one you live, and the smallness is theirs.
understanding.mechanism_label: Being seen as less than you are

weeks: Being told you will be erased

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on acting free of ego, like and dislike, in your own way.
verse.sanskrit: श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात् । स्वधर्मे निधनं श्रेयः परधर्मो भयावहः ॥
verse.line: Better your own path done imperfectly than someone else's done perfectly. Borrowed lives are dangerous.
verse.translation: Better is one's own duty, even done imperfectly, than the duty of another well done. Better is death in one's own duty; the duty of another is full of fear.
verse.why: Your own path, imperfectly walked, beats a borrowed one.
verse.misuse: Not 'stay in the role your family or birth assigned you'. It's about being true to your own nature and calling.

matched.label: I want to change careers but I'm scared

prasang.title: The ignorant and the wise; act free of like and dislike
prasang.summary: Krishna contrasts the attached and the wise, warns that ego claims credit for what nature does, and says to follow your own path rather than imitate another's.
prasang.lesson: Your own path, imperfectly walked, beats a borrowed one.

verse.meaning: Krishna tells Arjuna that it is better to follow your own path, even if you stumble, than to wear another person's life like a borrowed coat. He says that acting against your own nature brings fear, while acting in your own way, even imperfectly, keeps you whole. The choice is not between being perfect and being wrong, but between being true to yourself and living someone else's script.
verse.for_you: The silence from your partner and the pressure from your in-laws are trying to hand you a smaller life than the one you built. This verse says that walking your own path, even with stumbles, is safer than stepping into a role that was never yours.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Right after naming the five causes of any action, Krishna warns about the person who ignores four of them.
verse.sanskrit: तत्रैवं सति कर्तारमात्मानं केवलं तु यः । पश्यत्यकृतबुद्धित्वान्न स पश्यति दुर्मतिः ॥
verse.line: If you think you alone made it happen, or alone made it fail, you're not seeing the whole picture.
verse.translation: That being so, whoever, through an untrained understanding, sees himself alone as the doer does not truly see.
verse.why: You are one cause among five; own your part, not the whole outcome.
verse.misuse: Not a way to dodge responsibility; you are still one of the five causes.

prasang.title: What makes an action happen
prasang.summary: Every action has five causes: the setting, the doer, the instruments, the efforts, and providence. Seeing oneself as the only doer is a mistake.
prasang.lesson: You are one cause among five; own your part, not the whole outcome.

verse.meaning: Krishna is speaking to Arjuna on the battlefield. After explaining that every action has five causes, Krishna points to the danger of thinking you are the only one responsible. If you believe you alone made something happen or alone caused it to fail, you are not seeing the whole picture.
verse.for_you: When others see only a role, their picture is their smallness and not your measure; the harm deepens only when their picture begins to replace your own.

verse.ref: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Draupadi and Yudhishthira
verse.speaker: Draupadi
verse.setting: Draupadi argues that waiting on fate is no plan: people must act.
verse.sanskrit: न त्वेवात्माऽवमन्तव्यः पुरुषेण कदाचन / न ह्यात्मपरिभूतस् भूतिर्भवति शोभना
verse.line: Never look down on yourself. Nothing good grows from self-contempt.
verse.translation: A person should never look down on himself. The one who despises himself never finds real prosperity.
verse.why: Do right for its own sake, then work as if it all depends on you.

prasang.title: Do right without reward, and keep working
prasang.summary: Draupadi questions a world where the good suffer; Yudhishthira answers that he does right because it is right, not for reward. Draupadi replies that effort still matters: fate rewards no one who waits.
prasang.lesson: Do right for its own sake, then work as if it all depends on you.

verse.for_you: What you are cannot be cut smaller by what they see; your worth was never theirs to grant, and standing in your own truth is itself the duty.

verse.speaker: Vidula
verse.setting: Queen Vidula rouses her son, who lies defeated and despairing after losing his kingdom.
verse.sanskrit: माऽऽत्मानमवमन्यस्व मैनमल्पेन बीभरः / मनः कृत्वा सुकल्याणं मा भैस्त्वं प्रतिसंहर
verse.line: Don't think less of yourself or settle for little. Set your mind on something good, and stop fearing.
verse.translation: Do not hold yourself in contempt, and do not keep it going on too little. Set your mind on what is truly good; don't be afraid. Pull yourself together.
verse.why: Past failure doesn't define you. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.

prasang.title: Vidula rouses her defeated son
prasang.summary: Kunti sends Yudhishthira the old story of Queen Vidula, who finds her son lying defeated after losing his kingdom. She shames, then reasons, then encourages him until he rises and fights for it again.
prasang.story_hook: A prince lay in bed after losing everything, until his mother walked in and refused to let him stay there.
prasang.lesson: Past failure doesn't define you. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.

verse.for_you: The self cannot be cut, burned or made less; what they see is a role, and you were never only a role.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna on three kinds of food, effort, speech and giving.
verse.sanskrit: अनुद्वेगकरं वाक्यं सत्यं प्रियहितं च यत् । स्वाध्यायाभ्यसनं चैव वाङ्मयं तप उच्यते ॥
verse.line: Speak words that don't wound, that are true, kind and helpful. That is discipline of speech.
verse.translation: Speech that causes no distress, that is truthful, pleasant and beneficial, and the regular study of sacred texts: this is called austerity of speech.
verse.why: Speak kindly and truly, give without strings, and drop the show.
verse.misuse: Kind speech doesn't mean avoiding hard truths; it means saying them without cruelty.

matched.label: I have to give someone bad news

prasang.title: Three kinds of food, offering, austerity and giving
prasang.summary: Food, offering, austerity and giving each come in three kinds. Speech should be true, kind and helpful; giving should expect nothing back; effort for show doesn't last.
prasang.lesson: Speak kindly and truly, give without strings, and drop the show.

verse.meaning: Krishna speaks to Arjuna about the discipline of speech, telling them to use words that are true, kind, and helpful. This means speaking without causing distress, offering the truth gently without cruelty. It is about giving freely without expecting anything in return and letting go of performing for others. The idea is that speech should heal and clarify, not wound or flatter, and that true giving is done quietly without strings attached.
verse.for_you: Speak the true thing gently and firmly, hold your ground on what is yours, and do your own duty without shrinking to fit the picture they hold.

verse.speaker: Ram
verse.setting: Ram is struck by how Hanuman, a stranger and envoy, has just spoken to them.
verse.sanskrit: अविस्तरमसंदिग्धमविलम्बितमव्यथम्। उरःस्थं कण्ठगं वाक्यं वर्तते मध्यमस्वरम्॥
verse.line: Not too long, not vague, not rushed, not strained, in an even voice: that is how to speak.
verse.translation: His words were not long-winded, not ambiguous, not rushed, not strained; they came from the chest and throat in an even, middle tone.
verse.why: Fear jumps ahead of facts; calm, clear words build trust fast.

prasang.title: Sugriva's fear and Hanuman's first words
prasang.summary: The exiled Sugriva sees two armed strangers and panics, sure his brother has sent assassins. Hanuman calms him and goes in disguise to find out. His speech to the brothers is so clear and gentle that Ram is moved and trusts him at once.
prasang.story_hook: Sugriva saw two archers walking towards his hill and was sure they had come to kill him.
prasang.lesson: Fear jumps ahead of facts; calm, clear words build trust fast.

verse.meaning: Ram has just watched Hanuman speak to the fearful monkey king Sugriva. Hanuman did not overwhelm him with long speeches, nor did he leave him guessing. He spoke with a steady, even voice from the chest. That is how words should move between people. When fear is loud, calm and clear speech builds trust faster than any proof. It is a discipline, not a trick, to let your voice stay level and your meaning land exactly where it should.
verse.for_you: Stand in your own truth and do your own duty from it; let their picture stay theirs, and let your conduct speak.

story.title: Gargi questions Yajnavalkya at Janaka's court
story.story_hook: In a hall full of the most learned men in the land, one woman stood up twice.
story.summary: King Janaka offers a thousand cows to the wisest scholar. Yajnavalkya claims them and is challenged by one learned man after another. Gargi, the only woman, rises twice like a warrior with two arrows, then graciously tells the hall none of them can beat him. Yajnavalkya closes by asking what root a person grows from when cut down by death.
story.lesson: Ask your hard questions bravely, and give credit where it is due.

anchor.speaker: Yajnavalkya
anchor.setting: At King Janaka's debate, Kahola asks about the self.
anchor.sanskrit: या ह्येव पुत्रैषणा सा वित्तैषणा या वित्तैषणा सा लोकैषणोभे ह्येते एषणे एव भवतस्तस्माद्ब्राह्मणः पाण्डित्यं निर्विद्य बाल्येन तिष्ठासेत् । बाल्यं च पाण्डित्यं च निर्विद्याथ मुनिरमौनं च मौनं च निर्विद्याथ ब्राह्मणः ।
anchor.line: Wanting children, wanting money, wanting status: it is one desire. Learn, then live with a child's simplicity.
anchor.translation: The desire for sons is the desire for wealth, and the desire for wealth is the desire for worlds; both are just desires. So a wise man, having done with learning, should seek to live like a child. Having done with both childlike simplicity and learning, he becomes a sage; having done with both silence and its absence, he becomes a true knower.
anchor.why: Ask your hard questions bravely, and give credit where it is due.

prasang.title: Gargi questions Yajnavalkya at Janaka's court
prasang.summary: King Janaka offers a thousand cows to the wisest scholar. Yajnavalkya claims them and is challenged by one learned man after another. Gargi, the only woman, rises twice like a warrior with two arrows, then graciously tells the hall none of them can beat him. Yajnavalkya closes by asking what root a person grows from when cut down by death.
prasang.story_hook: In a hall full of the most learned men in the land, one woman stood up twice.
prasang.lesson: Ask your hard questions bravely, and give credit where it is due.

story.hook_title: Gargi, the only woman in the hall, stood up twice to question the wisest man there
story.teaser: Gargi, the only woman in the hall, stood up twice to question the wisest man there
story.for_you: Gargi did not lower her voice or soften her demand when the room was full of men. You already know the questions you could ask. Trust that the strength to ask them is already in your hands, and let it guide you.

weeks.title: Being told you will be erased

script: You are being erased. You built a CA practice from zero, and now your in-laws are drawing a smaller picture of you than the one you live. Your partner changes the subject, and the silence is quietly furious. You are not asking for too much.

On the battlefield, Arjuna is paralyzed by doubt. He is a warrior who has been told to lay down his bow. He feels the weight of expectations and the fear of doing the wrong thing. Krishna sees him hesitating. He sees Arjuna trying to wear a role that no longer fits. And Krishna replied:
श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात्, स्वधर्मे निधनं श्रेयः परधर्मो भयावहः.
In plain words: Better your own path done imperfectly than someone else's done perfectly. Borrowed lives are dangerous.

Krishna tells Arjuna that it is better to follow your own path, even if you stumble, than to wear another person's life like a borrowed coat. He says that acting against your own nature brings fear, while acting in your own way, even imperfectly, keeps you whole. This is not about being perfect. It is about being true to your own nature and calling. A borrowed life is dangerous because it asks you to step out of the truth of who you are.

Your in-laws and your partner are trying to hand you a smaller life than the one you built. This verse says that walking your own path, even with stumbles, is safer than stepping into a role that was never yours. You do not have to accept the smaller picture they are drawing. You are living a life you earned. That is your duty, and it is enough.
What is your own path asking of you today?

depth.life: You built a CA practice from nothing. Now your in-laws and partner want you to walk away for the baby, while your husband changes the subject. You feel erased and furious. This verse is for that moment of being handed a smaller picture of yourself than the one you live.
depth.points: The verse points out that a borrowed life is full of fear. Your partner's silence and your in-laws' pressure are trying to place you into a duty that is not yours. Walking your own path, even imperfectly, is better than performing someone else's role perfectly.
depth.practice: Look at the phone. Write down one sentence about what you actually want to do tomorrow, without asking anyone's permission.
depth.question: What does your own path look like when no one is watching?
